card.name: Who must supervise or give the drug
card.fires_on: Words in phrases saying a drug must be given or supervised by a qualified professional, such as 'suitably qualified', 'healthcare providers who', 'by persons trained'. It fires on the word just before the qualification is stated.

modes.label: Qualified professional
modes.description: The word 'qualified' or the people word (provider, persons, who) in a phrase about who may use or give the product.
modes.example: PE in medically unsupervised situations should receive appropriate training and instruction on the proper use of OMNITROPE from the physician or other suitably<< qualified>> health professional.

modes.label: Supervised by a provider
modes.description: Words like 'healthcare provider' after 'should be supervised by' before a skill requirement.
modes.example: Administration of VIMIZIM should be supervised by a healthcare<< provider>> knowledgeable in the management of hypersensitivity reactions

modes.label: Responsibility or judgment of someone
modes.description: Small words like 'the' or 'a' after 'responsibility of', 'judgment of' or 'determined by' that lead to a named person or body.
modes.example: administration should be determined by<< a>> physician experienced in intravenous fluid therapy.

card.plain: It lights up in sentences saying only trained, qualified professionals should give or oversee a drug.
